findings.title: `sed -i ''` only works on macOS/BSD sed
findings.body: On GNU sed (Linux, CI, WSL) `-i ''` treats the empty string as the input file name. The command fails with an error and `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is never updated when it already exists in the env file. The script still prints the success message afterwards. Use a portable form, for example `sed -i.bak -E ... && rm -f "$ENV_FILE.bak"`.

findings.title: Cache deletion does not refresh the status
findings.body: The delete-cache mutation never invalidates `connectedCalendars`, unlike the disconnect mutation, which has an `onSettled` that does. The "Last updated" entry and the delete option therefore stay on screen after a successful delete. They disappear only if the optional `onSuccess` callback happens to refetch. Add `await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` to the success or settled handler. Move `const utils` above the mutation.

findings.title: Unrelated tunnel/webhook dev script added
findings.body: The request covers calendar cache status and delete actions. This new script starts a tunnelmole tunnel and rewrites `../.env`. That is local dev tooling the request does not mention. The same applies to the `dev:cron` change from `ts-node` to `npx tsx` in `apps/web/package.json`. Drop both or move them to a separate PR.

findings.title: Unrelated dev:cron runner change
findings.body: Switching `dev:cron` from `ts-node` to `npx tsx` has nothing to do with the calendar cache feature. `npx` can also download `tsx` at run time if it is not a dependency. Revert it or move it to its own PR.

findings.title: Timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
findings.body: `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's locale. The surrounding string is translated, but the date is always shown in US format. Use the user's locale, for example `i18n.language`, from `useLocale`.

findings.title: Plain Error used instead of TRPCError
findings.body: A missing or foreign credential throws a generic `Error`. tRPC turns that into a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN, so the client cannot tell an access problem from a server fault. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` or `FORBIDDEN`.

held.title: The hand-edited DEFAULT NOW() probably doesn't match the Prisma schema, and it stamps old cache rows as just refreshed.
held.body:
The generated warning in this file says Prisma created this column with no default. Someone then added `DEFAULT NOW()` by hand. This causes two problems:

1. **Schema drift:** If `schema.prisma` declares `updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt` without `@default(now())`, the database no longer matches the schema. The next `prisma migrate dev` will detect the drift and generate a migration that drops the default again. I couldn't see the `schema.prisma` change to confirm this.
2. **Wrong cache status:** Every existing `CalendarCache` row gets the deploy time as `updatedAt`. The new `cacheUpdatedAt` status in the UI will then show stale caches as updated just now until each one is actually rewritten.

Fix: add `@default(now())` next to `@updatedAt` in `schema.prisma` so the schema and the migration agree. Better still, backfill existing rows with a value that reflects their real age, or leave the column nullable so the UI can show "unknown" for old rows.
